chapter: Harry Parker's, the district and its characters
title: Did women in the district sing? Lessie, Esther Bijou and Lila Bolden
summary: Dawson says the hustling women had talent but did not sing professionally; the two go back over Ann Cook, a violent woman called Lessie, and women who recorded.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well we can ask you about something else. Well what about those women, those hustling women, did many of them sing?
No, there wasn't nothing about, you know, singing. All they could get off a man, that's all they was after. It was stuck by North Sea.
Weren't there some places around here where they would have like maybe a piano guitar player who would sing like blues numbers?
Oh, when they'd have little, little Passovers like that, that's, you know, come in and some of them, a whole lot of them women could play piano too.
Yeah.

They had talent, but they didn't convert it into nothing, you know, wasn't making no use of it, you know. They just, uh, would, uh, could do that just for an effort, pleasure, you know, pastime like that.
I wonder how they got the idea to record Ann Cook, if they didn't know what others
sing.
I don't know, but she was a well-known woman, but... How come Ann Cook was well, how, how come you know about Ann Cook if she wasn't a singer?
Well I, all I knew was Ann Cook up in the district, you know, that's all I knew about
my...
But she used to be in the hostel now?
Yeah.
Oh yeah, just well... I lived, I lived right up down there on Liberty, between Gravy and Peter.
Well I heard, I heard that she killed seven men with her bare hands.
Yeah, of course she was. That may not be true. Well maybe not all at once. No, I don't be so chipped all, but...
Uh, she was tough, I tell you that.

Now we had, we had a woman, we had a woman from her, did you hear anything about Lessie? A woman called Lessie, was from up there? No, no. She was in the, she was in that bunch with Ann Cook and him. Yeah. She killed the woman on Gravy between, between Franklin and Saratoga. Yeah?
Yeah.
Cut her, cut her wide open.
What about Esther Bijoux, do you know her? Bijoux? She was a little good girl, yeah. Esther.
Esther.
Esther Bijoux.
Esther. Esther. Esther.
Yeah. I think she's kind of Danny Barclan. She sang, she made a record with, uh, Piron? Piron, I think, I think she's kind of Danny Barclan. Yeah.

And they had Lila Bolden, she recorded back there then. You ever heard of her? Bolden? Wasn't there a lot of Syracuse? Yeah. Did you know, uh, or at another profession? Yeah. They had two professions, a lot of them.
